questions.q: What are the three main types of media discussed in this chapter?
questions.a: The three types are Print, Electronic, and Digital media. A student who misses one type likely hasn't grasped the classification system and needs to review the basic definitions.

questions.q: Why is print media still considered important in rural India even though we have smartphones?
questions.a: Print media remains important because it does not rely on electricity or high-speed internet access to function. A student who says "it's faster" is incorrect, as print media is actually slower to distribute than digital media.

questions.q: If you are reading a news story on a website using your laptop, which category of media are you using?
questions.a: You are using digital media. If the student answers "electronic," they are confusing devices (like a laptop) with the method of transmission (internet/data), suggesting they need to distinguish between the hardware and the network.

questions.q: Compare the speed of news delivery between print media and electronic media. Which is faster?
questions.a: Electronic media (TV/Radio) is faster because it transmits news in real-time or near real-time, whereas print media requires a printing and physical delivery process. A student who struggles here may not understand the logistical difference between broadcasting and physical printing.

questions.q: Is a magazine considered digital media? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, a traditional magazine is print media because it is physically printed on paper. If a student says "yes," they are likely confusing "magazines" with "online blogs" or "e-magazines," showing a need for clarification on the medium of delivery.

questions.q: Create a plan for a small town that has no internet access to receive information about a new government rule. Which media type would be most effective?
questions.a: The most effective would be print media (newspapers/leaflets) or electronic media (radio). A poor answer would suggest an app or website, ignoring the lack of internet connectivity mentioned in the prompt.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Media refers to the various channels or tools used to ______ information to a large number of people, categorized into print, electronic, and digital formats.
Fill in the blank: Think about how you learned about the weather this ______ or the latest cricket score.
What is Media? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Media refers to the various channels or tools used to communicate information to a large number of people, categorized into print, electronic, and digital formats.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Media?
questions.a: Students often think "Electronic" and "Digital" are the same thing because both use electricity.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to correctly categorize a given media example (e.g., a newspaper vs. a news app) into its correct type and explain one unique characteristic of that category.
